tool.name: fastan
tool.description: FASTAN tandem-repeat arrays as content-annotated BED6
tool.command: set -o pipefail && #if str($input.ext) == 'fasta.gz' gunzip -c '$input' #else cat '$input' #end if | awk '/^>/{print;next}{print toupper(\$0)}' > in.fa && FAtoGDB in.fa gdb || true ; FasTAN -m -p -T\${GALAXY_SLOTS:-4} gdb && ONEview gdb.1ano | awk -f '$__tool_directory__/ano2bed6.awk' | LC_ALL=C sort -k1,1 -k2,2n > '$output'
tool.help:
**FASTAN** (Gene Myers) — tandem-array finder. Detects tandem repeats and partitions them into units. Emitted as **BED6**: name = ``u<unit_size>`` (tandem unit length), score = unit identity (0-1000 grayscale), strand = real orientation. Complementary to the DUST/low-complexity tracks. Pipeline: ``FAtoGDB`` -> ``FasTAN -m -p`` (.1ano) -> ``ONEview`` + awk. NOT ``ANOtoBED``, which reports contig-relative coordinates under the scaffold name (see check_coordinates.py). Input is upper-cased first.
⛔ **COLUMNS 4 AND 5 DO NOT MEAN THE SAME THING AS IN THE dustmasker, windowmasker AND tantan TRACKS.** Those three pipe through ``lc_classify.py``, which names a SEQUENCE SIGNATURE (``polyA``, ``(AT)n``, ``lc``) and scores PURITY x 1000. This tool names the repeat UNIT LENGTH (``u65``, ``u8``) and scores 1000 - 10 x divergence. Both are 0-1000 and higher-is-better, so a UCSC hub renders all four happily -- but grouping by name, or comparing scores, ACROSS tracks is mixing two vocabularies and nothing errors.
⛔ **``lc_classify.py`` IS ABSENT ON PURPOSE.** It brute-forces periods 1-6 only and returns ``lc`` for anything longer. Measured on 103,341 real intervals (ASM1303036v1), **75.9% have a unit longer than 6** -- 65,084 of them 20 bp or more, median interval 62 bp, longest 22,755. FASTAN measures the unit from its own tandem-array model (the ``L`` record) and reports divergence (``X``); classifying that would fail on three quarters of the intervals and replace a measured value with a guess. The UDT port omits it for the same reason, so the two stay in step.
